extraction.name: Visual Genome
extraction.description: A dataset of images densely annotated with numerous region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, and question answer pairs to enable the modeling of cognitive tasks and comprehensive scene understanding.
extraction.creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bemstein, Li Fei-Fei
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Visual Genome was collected and verified entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk. Workers were asked to draw bounding boxes, write region descriptions, extract objects, add attributes, connect pairs of objects with relationships, and write pairs of questions and answers about the images.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 108,249 images from the intersection of the YFCC100M and MS-COCO datasets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in region descriptions and question answer pairs were canonicalized to WordNet synsets to reduce ambiguity.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text preprocessing included lowercasing, lemmatizing, stripping excess whitespace, and removing non-alphanumeric characters from attributes, relationships, and region descriptions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Workers were presented with images and asked to draw bounding boxes and write descriptions for regions. Subsequent workers extracted objects from these descriptions and grounded them with bounding boxes. Workers then added attributes to objects and connected pairs of objects with relationships based on the text. Finally, workers wrote freeform and region-based question-answer pairs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All data went through a verification stage using majority voting (at least two out of three workers verifying correctness) and rapid judgments for objects to eliminate incorrectly labeled data, vague descriptions, or subjective/opinionated text.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: An average of 42 region descriptions, 21 objects, 16 attributes, 18 relationships, and 17 question-answer pairs per image.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers. Geographic distribution: United States 93.02%, Philippines 1.29%, Kenya 1.13%, India 0.94%, Russia 0.50%, Canada 0.47%, Others 2.65%. Gender: 54.15% male, 45.85% female. Age: Majority between 25 and 34 years old (range 18 to 68).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford's dependency parser (Stanford CoreNLP) was used to extract nouns automatically and send them to workers as suggestions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people. Certain sports (e.g., skiing, surfboarding) are also overrepresented due to a bias in the source images.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The canonicalization mappings to WordNet are not perfect and still contain some ambiguity. The dataset inherits subject matter biases from its source images.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and benchmarking computer vision models for comprehensive scene understanding, image search, visual question answering, robotic interactions, dense image captioning, and relationship extraction.
